name: William Orbit
notes: Filtered-analogue electronica applied to pop vocals — the late-90s ambient-pop upgrade: 90–120 straight with the backbeat on 2&4. Harmony is "modal, pedal-based — sus2/sus4 pads over a static bass; two-chord alternations and Dorian/Aeolian colour; the harmony rarely resolves", which is `susSubstitutionProb` at 0.52 (the highest in this section), `maxChords` 2, a vamp-weighted harmonic rhythm, and dorian and aeolian carrying the scales. Three drum deltas are quoted: "kick on 1 and the '&' of 3", "filtered 16th hats" (a pinned 16th with the velocity band pulled down, which is what filtering reads as to a note generator), and "long reverse-reverb tails" with percussion "treated as texture, often drenched and side-chained" — the `reverse` lane leading the percs at −9 dB, the quietest percussion block here. The bass is "filtered analogue synth bass, long notes with slow filter sweeps; occasional sub-only sections": `mirror_kick` at 0.9 with no glide. The melodic engine is not the vocal — "arpeggiated synth patterns and heavily filtered pads are the melodic engine, with the vocal placed dry against them" — so the counter is a high-ratio `arp` with a 1/16 echo and the lead sits low and sparse. "Extended instrumental outros are standard", which is the long outro in `sectionBars`. ⚠ `confidence` is medium because the research says so and marks the drum-placement specifics **[LOW-CONF]**: the gear, studio and credits are sourced, the grammar is inferred from the records. ⚠ Every drum probability here is **INFERRED**, as is `bpm.mode` 104. ⚠ **The bass is `mirror_kick` rather than the held `reese_sustain` the research describes** — *“filtered analogue synth bass, long notes with slow filter sweeps; occasional sub-only sections.”* — and that is a limit of the engine rather than a reading of the record. `generators::phrase_spans` re-articulates a held span only when it runs longer than two bars, so over the four-bar clip `reese_sustain` writes at most four notes and cannot reach the 500-bassline floor `engine/tests/bass.rs` holds every model to. `mobb-deep`, `dmx` and `capone-n-noreaga` carry the same substitution for the same reason; `followRootsProb` stays where it was so the line still reads as roots under the chord.
